## What

Follow-ups from the CodeRabbit review of #964, which merged before they were applied. All five findings are still open on develop; none were addressed pre-merge. Each is reachable from a caller-supplied value that plan-time validation let through.

## `engines.mismatch()`

**`page_size <= 0` crashed instead of declining.** It reached `128 % p` and raised `ZeroDivisionError`; a negative value passed the divisibility checks and reached `config_sm100._validate_params`, which raises. Now takes the same lower bound as `_validate_params`.

**The mixed-head-dim rejection asked the wrong question.** It keyed on head-dim inequalities, which is not the same as which flavor the lowering picks. Now keyed on `_pick_flavor`:

| dims | flavor | wired? | old rule | review's suggestion | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (128, 192) | (256, 256) | yes | **rejected** | ok | ok |
| (192, 128) | (192, 128) | no | rejected | rejected | rejected |
| (256, 128) | (256, 256) | yes | ok | **rejected** | ok |

Worth flagging: the review suggested `d_qk > 128 and d_v <= 128`, which fixes `(128, 192)` but breaks `(256, 128)`. Only `(192, 128)` actually lands on the unwired d192x128, so the flavor is the thing to test.

## `_common_blackwell._resolve_seqlen_kv()`

Clamp the per-batch KV length to `[0, scalar_seqlen_kv]`, as `_resolve_seqlen_q` already does for Q — the KV twin lacking it was the asymmetry.

Load-bearing under `PAGED_KV`, where the scalar is the block table's capacity (`max_pages * PAGE_SIZE`): a device length above it put `n_pages_b` past the end of the table row, so the page walk read a block-table entry outside the batch's row and handed TMA an arbitrary page id. Clamping at the shared resolver covers every caller, including the per-tile loop update.

## `api_dsl.SdpaFwdDslSm100`

- **Block-table stride declarations must have two entries.** The execute-time comparison zips `got`/`want`/`shape`, and `zip` truncates — a one-element declaration silently skipped the page-axis check and still entered the compile key.
- **Reject paged operands from another CUDA device.** The launch device comes from `q_tensor` and the fake descriptors carry no device, so a pool or block table on a second GPU reached the binder as a foreign-device pointer.

## `graph_analyzer.SdpaBinding._build_index()`

Dedupe bound tensors by identity. One block table serving both K and V is the ordinary case; counting it twice marked its name and uid ambiguous, so `resolve_variant_pack` ignored variant-pack entries keyed by either.

## `SUPPORT_MATRIX_TRACKER.md`

The gaps row said paged KV was d128-forward only and listed THD as unsupported, contradicting footnote p and the d256 column.

## Validation

SM100, cuDNN 9.26.0.33, `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`:

- paged + graph-analyzer + split-kv suites: **247 passed**
- `test_mhas_v2 -k fwd`: 200 passed / 4 failed — those 4 (`fwd_unified_block_mask_L0` test11/12/20/23) reproduce **identically with these changes reverted**, so they predate this work.

## Not done

One review item is declined: replacing the set-union character in a test docstring for RUF002. There is no ruff hook in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and no `[tool.ruff]` config — the gates are clang-format, black and SPDX — and that character appears 68 times across 20 files, including 7 in the kernel #964 modified. Changing one test file would make it inconsistent with the established notation for a rule that is not enforced.

files.patch:
@@ -604,7 +604,7 @@ still declines THD (the wrapper's `cu_seqlen` path serves it).
 | d=64 MXFP8 / d=64 quantized THD | SM100, SM107 (exact-shape gates) |
 | Bias forward | SM100, SM107, SM120 |
 | Dropout, ALiBi, `block_mask`, `score_mod` | every arch, both passes |
-| Paged KV cache | every arch except SM100/SM103 f16/bf16 d128 forward (see ᵖ); fp8/mxfp8 pools, sink, THD, packed block tables everywhere |
+| Paged KV cache | every arch except SM100/SM103 f16/bf16 d128 / d256 forward (see ᵖ); fp8/mxfp8 pools, sink, packed block tables everywhere |
 
 ᵏ **THD / ragged forward layout.** Q/K/V/O must be BSHD-ordered over **(H, S, D)**
 only — head dim innermost, then heads, then tokens (`graph_analyzer.packed_layout_ok`).

@@ -575,6 +575,13 @@ def __init__(
         self.paged_max_seq_len_kv = None if paged_max_seq_len_kv is None else int(paged_max_seq_len_kv)
         self.paged_table_stride = None if paged_table_stride is None else tuple(int(s) for s in paged_table_stride)
         self.paged_table_v_stride = None if paged_table_v_stride is None else tuple(int(s) for s in paged_table_v_stride)
+        # A block table is (batch, max_pages), so its declared stride must name
+        # both axes. The execute-time comparison zips got/want/shape, and zip
+        # truncates -- a one-element declaration would silently skip the
+        # page-axis check and still enter the compile key.
+        for _name, _st in (("paged_table_stride", self.paged_table_stride), ("paged_table_v_stride", self.paged_table_v_stride)):
+            if _st is not None and len(_st) != 2:
+                raise ValueError(f"{_name} must have exactly two entries (batch, page); got {_st}")
 
         self.batch_size: Optional[int] = None
         self.s_q_max: Optional[int] = None

Preserve develop's `arr[cutlass.Int32(batch_idx)]` conversion inside the new clamp, since persistent payload readers can supply a raw arithmetic value. Validation: SM100, CuTe DSL 4.8, cuDNN 9.25.1: paged-KV, graph-analyzer and SM100 split-KV suites with explicit L0/L1 selection: 246 passed, one capture test excluded after reproducing its failure on both head and baseline. 18 focused contract checks cover shared-table object/name/uid binding, page-size boundaries, mixed-dimension eligibility, and empty/one-/three-entry stride declarations; 12 fail on baseline 8071aa151d9d and all 18 pass on this head. Three additional adapter checks reject foreign-device inputs before launch. A public-adapter probe with a 256-token table capacity and lengths 384, 257, negative, zero and valid values returns clamped reference O/LSE on this head. Backing storage deliberately contains valid guard-page IDs, allowing a safe baseline comparison: old code includes the extra page (e.g. O=1.0 versus the correct 0.5). Public graph API numerical checks pass for both newly admitted (D_QK,D_V)=(128,192) and (256,128), with GQA, partial pages and an empty batch; both select the SM100 FROST d256 route with split_kv=2. Small head/baseline/baseline/head spot check on the same SM100: FP16 paged decode, B=3,H=8,KV heads=2,D=128,Q length=1,page size=128,capacity=256,CGA=2,PackGQA. CPU enqueue medians overlap (baseline 21.88–23.00 us; head 22.82–23.33 us); captured GPU execution is 8.23 versus 8.30 us. Correctness, poisoned-output replay and changed-V replay passed; no material regression in this measured case.

Limitations: The existing capture test fails before the tested execute call: on the baseline, PyTorch capture_begin itself raises under synchronization-debug mode and then leaves capture cleanup failing. This is separate from the successful explicit-stream capture/replay probe above; it is not attributed to this PR. An isolated merge with develop c3b5b143da79 has the resolver conflict described above. No merged-tree GPU result or passing newly requested CI is claimed. Style check passed on this head. No independent SM103/Rubin performance result or sanitizer result; the performance spot check is one small workload, not a broad throughput benchmark.
